records.title: chore: bump bun to v1.3 and add minimumReleaseAge
records.body:
## Summary

Two related changes to harden the supply chain.

### 1. Bump bun to v1.3

`packageManager`: `bun@1.2.22` → `bun@1.3.14`. Required to use the `minimumReleaseAge` setting added in bun 1.3.

### 2. Add `minimumReleaseAge` to harden supply chain

New `bunfig.toml`:
```toml
[install]
minimumReleaseAge = 172800
minimumReleaseAgeExcludes = ["@nuxt/*", "@nuxtjs/*", "nuxt", "nuxt-*", "@vercel/*", "@ai-sdk/*", "ai"]
```

Sets a 2-day minimum age (172800 seconds) before any newly published dependency can resolve. Mitigates compromised-package attacks. Trusted-source allowlist exempts the Nuxt and Vercel ecosystems.

## Test plan
- [ ] `bun install` resolves cleanly with v1.3.14
- [ ] CI passes

records.title: ci: replace pull_request_target with pull_request and pin action SHAs
records.body:
## Summary

- Replaces `pull_request_target` with `pull_request` in `label-pr.yml` and `semantic-pull-request.yml` — eliminates the elevated-privilege trigger that could be abused if a `checkout` step were ever added
- Pins `amannn/action-semantic-pull-request` to commit SHA `48f256284bd46cdaab1048c3721360e808335d50` (v6) to prevent floating-tag supply chain attacks
- Pins `marocchino/sticky-pull-request-comment` to commit SHA `773744901bac0e8cbb5a0dc842800d45e9b2b405` (v2.9.4) for the same reason

Addresses security finding **VULN-10700**. Labelling and PR title validation are both read-only operations that work identically under `pull_request`.

## Test plan
- [ ] Open a test PR — label-pr workflow runs and applies the correct label
- [ ] Open a test PR with a non-conforming title — semantic-pull-request workflow posts the expected error comment

- Extends the AI context (AsyncLocalStorage) in `observe.ts` to carry `userId` and `tags` alongside the existing model wrapper
- Adds `buildProviderOptions(model, metadata)` and `buildGatewayProviderOptions(metadata)` to merge model fallbacks with gateway `user`/`tags` fields
- Updates all agent `prepareCall` methods (base, source, admin) to send gateway metadata on every request
- Updates standalone `generateText` calls (router, web search tools, title generation, OCR) to include gateway metadata
- Web chat routes set `userId` to the authenticated user's ID with the `web-chat` tag
- Bot adapter routes derive the tag from `context.platform` (e.g. `github-adapter`, `discord-adapter`) and send the message author's username as the user
- Supports Vercel AI Gateway's new reporting API for per-user and per-adapter usage tracking

Implemented Vercel Web Analytics for Nuxt application

## Summary
Successfully installed and configured @vercel/analytics package for the Savoir chat application.

## Changes Made

### 1. Package Installation
- Installed `@vercel/analytics@^1.6.1` package using bun
- Updated `apps/chat/package.json` to include the new dependency
- Updated `bun.lock` lockfile with all dependency resolutions

### 2. Code Changes to app.vue
- Added import statement: `import { Analytics } from '@vercel/analytics/nuxt'`
- Added `<Analytics />` component to the template, placed within the `<UApp>` component alongside other root components
- Preserved all existing code structure and functionality

## Files Modified

1. **apps/chat/app/app.vue**
   - Added Analytics import in the `<script setup>` section
   - Added Analytics component to the template after NuxtLayout

2. **apps/chat/package.json**
   - Added @vercel/analytics dependency

3. **bun.lock**
   - Updated with new dependency and its transitive dependencies

## Implementation Details

The Analytics component was placed inside the `<UApp>` component, after the `<NuxtLayout>` section. This ensures it's available throughout the entire application and will track page views and custom events across all routes.

The implementation follows Vercel's best practices for Nuxt integration:
- Using the Nuxt-specific export from `@vercel/analytics/nuxt`
- Placing the component at the root level for global tracking
- Maintaining compatibility with the existing application structure

## Verification

- ✅ Linter ran successfully with no errors on app.vue
- ✅ Package installed correctly with bun
- ✅ Code follows existing patterns and conventions
- ✅ All imports are properly typed for TypeScript
- ✅ Lockfile updated correctly

## Notes

The Analytics component will automatically:
- Track page views when users navigate between routes
- Work in both development and production environments
- Require VERCEL_ANALYTICS_ID environment variable in production (set automatically on Vercel)
- Be a no-op in development unless explicitly configured

No additional configuration is needed - the analytics will start working automatically when deployed to Vercel.

##### Fixed `drizzle-kit pull` bugs when using Gel extensions.

Because Gel extensions create schema names containing `::` (for example, `ext::auth`), Drizzle previously handled these names incorrectly. Starting with this release, you can use Gel extensions without any problems. Here’s what you should do:

1. Enable extensions schemas in `drizzle.config.ts`

```ts
import  { defineConfig } from "drizzle-kit";

export default defineConfig({
  dialect: 'gel',
  schemaFilter: ['ext::auth', 'public']
});
```
